text.p: U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) conditions for approving the merger of Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG into Novartis AG NOVZn.S leave the company's innovative potential intact, the companies said.
"The required divestments and conditions will leave the innovative potential of Novartis intact," they said in a joint statement.
An agreement with the FTC addressed three areas where there was an overlap of business in North America: corn herbicides, flea and tick control products and gene therapy.
Novartis will divest Sandoz's corn herbicide and animal health business with combined 1996 sales of $390 million.
In gene therapy, Novartis agreed to provide access to HSV-tk technology for cancer treatment and ex-vivo gene therapy covered by a broad U.S. patent.
It will also provide access to Factor VIII for haemophilia gene therapy and cytokines for use in cell expansion for ex-vivo gene therapy.
"Novartis retains royalty rights and will have a cross-licence option from potential licencees in HSV-tk gene therapy and cytokines," it said.
